summary: Qian Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Lin studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and earned a PhD from the University of Washington under Collett Cox, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and others.

Qiang Ning is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who earned a doctorate under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. Ning taught at Yale, San Diego State, and the University of Michigan, and held a research post at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology, studying at Xuehai Tang, National Tsing Hua University, and under Youwei Kang. He held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, Translation Bureau, Tsinghua University, Nankai University, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji and Zhongxin Jiang, earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, and was a professor at Peking University.

Qingying Chen was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Qinghai Nationalities University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He held posts at Delingha High School, Qinghai Academy of Social Sciences, and China Tibetology Research Center.
Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Zhu served as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and at the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

R. Balasubramanian was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. From around 1980 to 1989, he served as Director at the University of Madras.

R. Gordon Wasson studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics. Active in religious studies and Indology, he held posts at journalism outlets, the Guaranty Trust Company of New York, J.P. Morgan & Co., and the American Council of Learned Societies.

R. H. Tawney was an historian who studied at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1917–1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).
R. P. Paranjpye studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

R. Sathyanarayana was an Indologist who earned a master's degree in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

R. Thangaswami Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. He held posts at Presidency College, the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was Honorary Professor at Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

R. Venkatraman studied history, archaeology, and Indology at Madurai Kamaraj University, earning a PhD supervised by N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan. He served as a Reader at Madurai Kamaraj University (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore was a philosopher and religious studies figure who studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London. He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. She was appointed as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool around 2014.

Rachel H. Pang works in religious studies, Tibetology, and sinology, holding a PhD from the University of Virginia. She served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her doctoral dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay. She held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).
